findings.text: review_scope sets _COMPOSED_UNITS directly (_COMPOSED_UNITS.set(...)) where its sibling _REVIEW_SECTIONS is only ever set inside the reviewing_sections context manager, which resets both on exit. Every production path is safe because crew_dispatch_commands.py:3128 wraps the composition in reviewing_sections, but review_scope is public and takes an explicit sections parameter, so a direct caller on an unreviewed plan leaves the widened tuple set in its context; a later write_review_sidecar call with no traced_units in that same context would then stamp every unit as traced for a record whose composition never widened. The test seam is exactly the pattern at tests/test_a_review_round_is_section_scoped.py:109, where the context manager is used deliberately, so nothing fails today. Wrapping the set in a token reset owned by the caller, or having review_scope return the decided units rather than side-effect them, removes the latent cross-composition carry.
